passage:
An empty lot in the city was turned into a community garden. Residents grew vegetables, flowers, and herbs.
After a few years, a company wanted to build apartments there. Some people supported the plan because the city needed housing. Others wanted to keep the garden because it gave neighbors green space and food.
The city held a public discussion. Students attending the meeting saw that both sides had real reasons.
The final plan included apartments and a smaller garden on the ground floor.
The decision was not perfect for anyone. But it taught students that city planning is often about balancing needs, not choosing between good and bad.
